name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text:
**Decision:** Create a single, shared “decision log” that every department can read and add to in real time.

**Why it’s best:** Right now, each team makes choices in silos and then has to re-explain them to others. A shared log turns every decision into a reusable artifact that saves time, prevents repeats, and keeps everyone aligned without extra meetings. The trade-off is we accept a small upfront cost in agreeing on a simple format and a lightweight moderation rule—nothing fancy, just “who decided what and why.”

name: Scriv
text: I'm not convinced that a shared decision log is the best use of our resources, as it could lead to information overload and make it difficult to discern important decisions from trivial ones. A better alternative might be to implement a regular, cross-departmental meeting where key decisions are discussed and summarized, allowing for more nuanced communication and clarification. What would settle this argument for me is data on how often teams currently re-explain decisions to each other, and how much time that really costs us.

name: Chisel
text:
**Decision:** Adopt a lightweight “decision digest” that every department can post to once a week—one paragraph per choice, with a one-word label (Impact: High/Med/Low).

**Why it’s best:** It keeps the shared log from drowning in noise while still giving everyone a fast way to see what others are deciding. A weekly pulse beats endless meetings and still beats siloed notes.

**Trade-off:** We accept that some fast-moving decisions might wait a week to be logged, so we lose a tiny bit of immediacy for a lot more clarity.

name: Sift
text: I'm not convinced that a weekly "decision digest" is the way to go, as it may still lead to outdated information and a lack of transparency into the decision-making process. A better alternative might be to implement a dynamic, hierarchical system that allows departments to categorize and prioritize their decisions in real-time, making it easier to filter out noise and focus on high-impact choices. This approach would settle the argument if we could see a prototype that demonstrates its effectiveness in reducing information overload while maintaining the integrity of the decision log.
